PASS — commit 4381632. Realized P&L on moving weighted-average cost: a SELL releases qty x avg_cost taken before the quantity drops. Not FIFO, and the reason matters — the open side has folded on average cost since bd:shotockviz-msg, so FIFO on the realized side would put two halves of one book on two cost flows and realized+unrealized would stop reconciling; and transactions.date is a DATE with no lot id, so a FIFO answer would depend on whatever row order Postgres returned for same-day trades. Two grains reported because they are different numbers: RealizedSale per SELL (ledger truth) and ClosedTrade per round trip (what a trader reads). Win/loss judged in THB because a USD gain can be a THB loss. profit_factor is None with no losses — undefined, not infinite. Explicitly not tax output; the endpoint says so. WONTFIX — not worth doing, on Felix's own assessment and his own earlier tier. I asked him to measure whether the error is reachable at this book's scale before migrating, and to treat a well-argued 'no' as a valid outcome. It is a no.
THE NUMBER: every money field leaves the API through round(x, 2) (37 round() calls in api/routes/portfolio.py), so the decision threshold is half a satang, 0.005 THB. Worst-case float error on total_value, derived: u = 2^-53 = 1.11e-16; recursive summation over ~50 rows at 1e7 THB plus 60 positions at 2e7 THB totals <= ~3.4e-6 THB. Margin ~1,470x adversarial, ~12,000x random-walk. Inverted: the book would need ~9.0e11 THB (~USD 27bn) of gross lifetime turnover before the bound reaches half a satang.
WHY THE BOUND HOLDS: build_holdings is a pure fold over raw transactions on every read and NO derived money is persisted anywhere — Transaction is the only table carrying user money across all 17 Base subclasses; cost_basis/total_value are Pydantic response models, not ORM. Error is bounded per read, not accumulated across reads.
WHY MIGRATING WOULD BE WORSE, verified by Oliver in the source: portfolio_service.py:718-719, 736, 865, 888 do float(t.qty), float(t.price), float(fee), float(raw) — switching the column to Numeric returns Decimal which those lines immediately downcast back to float, so the migration alone changes ZERO output while paying a table rewrite on the user's real rows. Worse, it would make bd:shotockviz-tmz LESS exact: avg_cost = cost_basis/qty and the SELL path releases qty*avg; 1000/3 is inexact in binary AND in decimal, and under Decimal the released amount would no longer equal the cost_basis removed unless an explicit residual-absorption rule is also written. Same for eb1's qty*price invariant — a 3:1 split is inexact in base 10 too; only exact rationals buy that invariant.
REVISIT IF: a derived money value gets persisted (materialised holdings, cached realized P&L) — the per-read bound dies instantly; or the product starts emitting numbers someone reconciles against (broker export, tax output, bookkeeper CSV); or crypto lands in the portfolio and 8-decimal quantities meet 2-decimal money. The expand-contract sequence is recorded in the bead notes for whoever overrules this.
